title: Canonical localization filtration descends to filtered derived objects
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion with complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring. Use the ordinary abelian categories of sheaves of modules over the constant ring $\Lambda$ on the small etale sites [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Here inverse image, direct image and extension by zero are those of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. The bounded filtered derived localization means bounded cochain complexes with finite decreasing filtrations by subcomplexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-sp-filtration, def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients], localized at chain maps inducing quasi-isomorphisms on every graded complex. Suppose that $j^{-1}$, $i^{-1}$, $j_!$ and $i_*$ are exact and that, for every bounded complex $B^\bullet$ of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$, the degreewise localization sequence
$$0\to j_!j^{-1}B^\bullet\to B^\bullet\to i_*i^{-1}B^\bullet\to0,$$
formed from the counit of $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ and the unit of $i^{-1}\dashv i_*$, is exact. The assignment
$$F^0B^\bullet=B^\bullet,\qquad F^1B^\bullet=j_!j^{-1}B^\bullet,\qquad F^2B^\bullet=0$$
sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms on every associated graded complex. It therefore descends to a functorial section of the forgetful functor from the bounded filtered derived localization to the bounded derived category. The descended filtered object is canonically independent of the chosen representative, and its graded pieces are $i_*i^{-1}B^\bullet$ in degree $0$ and $j_!j^{-1}B^\bullet$ in degree $1$.

source.place: Example 5.2.3, construction of the canonical filtered object

proof.text: For a bounded sheaf complex B, the counit j_!j^{-1}B → B is natural in B, so its degreewise images form a subcomplex. Using the given exact localization sequence, define F^0B=B, F^1B=j_!j^{-1}B and F^2B=0 (with F^pB=B for p≤0 and F^pB=0 for p≥2). This is a finite decreasing filtration by subcomplexes, and its graded complexes are the quotient B/(j_!j^{-1}B) and j_!j^{-1}B.

source.place: Example 5.2.3, construction of the section on C^b(Sh(X,Λ))

proof.text: A chain map f:B→C preserves the displayed filtration because the counit is natural, and identities and composites are preserved, so this assignment is a functor on filtered complexes. If f is a quasi-isomorphism, exactness of j^{-1} and j_! carries the induced map on F^1 to a quasi-isomorphism. The degreewise short exact localization sequences identify the map on the quotient graded complex with i_*i^{-1}f; exactness of i^{-1} and i_* makes this a quasi-isomorphism as well. Hence the filtered map is a filtered quasi-isomorphism. Indeed, an exact additive functor T preserves kernels, images and cokernels, so H^n(TB)=T(H^nB), naturally in chain maps; this proves both quasi-isomorphism assertions directly.

source.place: Example 5.2.3, exactness of j^* and j_! and descent

proof.text: First verify that forgetting filtration inverts every graded quasi-isomorphism w:K→L, not just maps produced by the section. Give M=Cone(w) the componentwise filtration F^pM=F^pL⊕F^pK[1]. Its grade is Cone(gr^p w), hence acyclic by the cone criterion. Choose common finite filtration bounds a,b for K,L. Starting with F^{b+1}M=0, the long exact cohomology sequences of 0→F^{p+1}M→F^pM→gr^pM→0 show by downward induction that each F^pM is acyclic; thus M=F^aM is acyclic and w is an ordinary quasi-isomorphism. The universal property of localization now gives the forgetful functor ω and, using Step 2, the section S. On complexes ωS is the identity, and the same holds on formal inverses of quasi-isomorphisms, so ωS=id in the formal-localization model. For other equivalent localization models this is the canonical natural isomorphism supplied by the universal property.

source.place: §5.1.2(a)–(b) and Example 5.2.3; forgetful descent expanded as in Stacks derived.tex, lemma-filtered-derived-functors, using the finite-filtration cone argument, homology.tex Lemma 0117, and categories.tex Lemma 04VG

proof.text: Apply S to a specified derived isomorphism between two representatives. The factorization in Step 3 makes the resulting filtered isomorphism functorial in that specified isomorphism, with its underlying map the original one. Thus independence of representatives is relative to the chosen identifications with the derived object; no uniqueness of isomorphisms between unmarked representatives is asserted. On complexes the assumed short exact sequence identifies B/(j_!j^{-1}B) with i_*i^{-1}B naturally in B, and gr^1 is j_!j^{-1}B. Exactness shows these two termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms (Step 2); grading also inverts graded quasi-isomorphisms by definition. The natural quotient identifications therefore descend by the localization universal property. Hence gr^0 S(B)≅i_*i^{-1}B and gr^1 S(B)≅j_!j^{-1}B naturally in the bounded derived category, with all other grades zero.

source.place: Example 5.2.3, graded pieces and representative independence
